input: Print and laminate a meal rotation chart for the fridge

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: The chart's structure depends entirely on whether it covers breakfast, lunch, dinner, or all meals — and whether it spans a week, two weeks, or a full month rotation.
Knowing who the chart is for (a single person, a couple, a family with kids, etc.) determines how many meals or portions to include and whether dietary variety or restrictions matter.
The visual style — colour-coded, minimalist, illustrated, whiteboard-style for writing in meals — changes the design approach significantly.
Whether the user has home printing and laminating equipment or needs to use a print shop determines the workflow and file format needed.
The target paper size (A4, A3, Letter, etc.) affects layout design and laminating pouch sizing, and needs to be confirmed before designing.
Knowing whether the chart should be fully pre-filled with specific meals or left blank/writable changes whether meal content needs to be gathered first.
Understanding whether this is a fixed rotation (the same meals repeat automatically) or a flexible weekly planner changes how the chart is structured and labelled.

gold.taskTitle: Print and laminate a meal rotation chart for the fridge
gold.taskDescription: Create a printed and laminated meal rotation chart to be displayed on the fridge for ongoing household meal planning.

questions.title: Which meals does the chart need to cover?
questions.description: Determine whether the chart covers dinner only, or also breakfast and lunch, so the number of rows or sections can be defined.

questions.title: How many people is this chart planned for?
questions.description: Identify the household size and whether any members have dietary restrictions, which may influence how meals are labelled or grouped.

questions.title: Should the chart be pre-filled with meals or left writable?
questions.description: Clarify whether specific meals will be printed onto the chart, or whether it will be a blank template to fill in with a dry-erase or wet-erase marker after laminating.

questions.title: How many days or weeks should one rotation cycle span?
questions.description: Establish the rotation length (e.g. 7-day, 14-day, or monthly) so the correct number of columns or slots can be laid out.

questions.title: What paper size should the finished chart be?
questions.description: Confirm the target dimensions (A4, A3, US Letter, etc.) to ensure the design fits the laminating pouch and fridge space available.

questions.title: What visual style do you want the chart to have?
questions.description: Determine whether the user wants a clean minimal grid, a colour-coded layout, a decorative family-friendly design, or something else, to guide the design choices.

questions.title: Do you have a printer and laminator at home?
questions.description: Find out whether the user can print and laminate at home or needs to use an external print or office supply shop, which changes the steps and file format needed.
